question.text: Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs) issued by Indian companies must have a minimum maturity period of __________, and are regulated by RBI under FEMA guidelines.

explanation.text: The Logic: FCCBs issued by Indian companies are required to have a minimum maturity period of 5 years. They are regulated by RBI under FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act) guidelines. The expense limits are capped at 4% of the issue size for public issues and 2% for private placements. The Trap: The 3-year, 7-year, and 10-year options are common distractors for those who confuse FCCB maturity with other debt-instrument tenor norms. Note: The NISM XII workbook (pages 57-58) confirms the 5-year minimum maturity, RBI/FEMA regulation, and the 4% public / 2% private placement expense limits for FCCBs.
